subject: English – Grammar and Writing
status: DRAFT — for review by an English teacher before it is relied on
source: Drafted against the CBSE English Language and Literature (184) syllabus for 2025-26, Section B for Class IX: the grammar items (determiners, tenses, modals, subject–verb concord, reported speech) assessed through gap filling, editing and transformation, and the descriptive paragraph and story or diary entry writing tasks.
notes: Concept names carry the class, because the same grammar item is taught in both years and concept names must be unique across the curriculum.

outcomes.statement: Uses the articles a, an and the correctly, including before vowel sounds and with a noun already mentioned or unique.
Uses quantifiers such as some, any, much, many, few, a few, little and a little correctly with countable and uncountable nouns.
Identifies and corrects errors in the use of articles, demonstratives, possessives and quantifiers in a short passage.
Uses the simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous forms of the present, past and future correctly in context.
Selects the tense that a time expression or a sequence of events requires when filling gaps in a passage.
Identifies and corrects errors of tense and verb form in a short passage.
Uses modals such as can, could, may, might, must, should, ought to, will and would to express ability, permission, possibility, obligation and advice.
Selects the modal that matches the speaker's purpose in a given situation, such as a polite request or a strong obligation.
Identifies and corrects the misuse of modals in sentences and short passages.
Applies subject–verb agreement with singular, plural and collective subjects and with words such as each, every, either and neither.
Applies agreement rules when subjects are joined by and, or or neither…nor, or separated from the verb by a phrase.
Identifies and corrects errors of subject–verb agreement in a short passage.
Converts statements from direct to reported speech, changing tense, pronouns and words of time and place correctly.
Converts questions into reported speech, using if or whether or the question word, with statement word order.
Converts commands and requests into reported speech using verbs such as ordered, advised, requested and asked.
Describes a person, event or situation from visual or verbal cues in a well-organised paragraph of 100–120 words.
Uses sensory detail and precise vocabulary to give the reader a clear picture of what is described.
Writes a story from a given cue or title with a clear beginning, development and ending, in 100–120 words.
Writes a diary entry in the correct format that records an experience and reflects on personal feelings about it.
